jurisdiction.name: Caribbean Community
jurisdiction.overview: Official documents of this organisation are listed on its own page and are not counted in member countries' totals.

narrative.summary: The Caribbean Community's AI texts so far come from two of its institutions. The Caribbean Court of Justice issued a practice direction on the use of generative AI tools in proceedings before the Court in February 2025, and the Caribbean Examinations Council approved a regional policy framework on responsible generative AI in secondary education in December 2024. No AI declaration, framework or policy adopted by CARICOM organs has been found; a Caribbean AI Task Force convened by the Caribbean Telecommunications Union issued an advisory report in July 2026.
narrative.review_notes: The sites of the CARICOM Secretariat, the Caribbean Court of Justice, the Caribbean Examinations Council and the Caribbean Telecommunications Union were searched in a single pass. Pending: the Caribbean AI Task Force report and any outcome of the July 2026 Caribbean AI Forum, and an AI policy for courtrooms announced by the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court.

instruments.official_title: Practice Direction No. 1 of 2025: The Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence Tools in Court Proceedings
instruments.english_title: Practice Direction No. 1 of 2025: The Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence Tools in Court Proceedings
instruments.issuing_authority: Caribbean Court of Justice (President of the Court)
instruments.publisher_name: Caribbean Court of Justice (President of the Court)
instruments.current_status: In force from 14 February 2025, the date of issue, under its own commencement clause ('shall take effect from the date on which it is issued'); periodic revisions are foreseen. Applies to all proceedings before the Caribbean Court of Justice.
instruments.scope: All proceedings before the Caribbean Court of Justice, in its appellate and original jurisdictions.
instruments.summary: Issued under Part 18.1 of the CCJ (Appellate Jurisdiction) Rules 2024 and Part 32.1 of the CCJ (Original Jurisdiction) Rules 2024, it governs generative AI use by attorneys, parties, witnesses, self-represented persons and other users in all proceedings before the Caribbean Court of Justice. It bars GenAI for generating or rephrasing affidavits and witness statements (exhibits only with the Court's permission), makes users fully responsible for outputs, requires independent verification of GenAI citations, forbids entering sensitive, confidential or privileged information into open source GenAI tools, and lets the Court require disclosure of GenAI use; breaches can attract costs orders, rejection of documents or reduced evidentiary weight.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Court rules binding on attorneys, parties and witnesses who use generative AI in proceedings before the Caribbean Court of Justice.
instruments.evidence_reference: Read: the PDF on ccj.org (8 Nov 2026): title 'Practice Direction No. 1 of 2025: The Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence Tools in Court Proceedings'; issued by Adrian Saunders, President, under Part 18.1 (AJR 2024) and Part 32.1 (OJR 2024), 14 February 2025; 'This Practice Direction shall take effect from the date on which it is issued'; 'applies to all proceedings before the Caribbean Court of Justice'; 'Citations or references generated by GenAI tools must be independently verified using reliable sources.' CCJ news page https://ccj.org/ccj-issues-new-practice-direction ('CCJ Issues New Practice Direction', February 14, 2025) confirms. Same document found earlier in slices C-BHS-BRB-BLZ-CUB and C-DMA-GRD-GUY-HTI (proposed there under code 'CCJ'). | Independent check 2026-11-08: Every field matches the text. Court's own AI rules -> administrative_policy_mandatory_in_scope / judiciary per convention; in_force from issue date correct. No duplicate in briefs or data (no national record of it). applies_to: CCJ original jurisdiction covers CARICOM states party to the Agreement Establishing the CCJ; appellate jurisdiction Barbados, Belize, Dominica, Guyana, Saint Lucia (researcher's list; not re-read from ccj.org in this pass). Editors should limit applies_to to those states rather than all CARICOM members if the court's jurisdiction list is confirmed.

instruments.official_title: CXC Responsible Generative Artificial Intelligence Policy Framework for the Regional Secondary Education System
instruments.english_title: CXC Responsible Generative Artificial Intelligence Policy Framework for the Regional Secondary Education System
instruments.current_status: Cover dated November 2024; 'Approved by the CXC Board of Governors at its Annual Meeting of Council on 6 December 2024'. Guidance for regional and national education actors; not binding on governments.
instruments.scope: Secondary education and CXC assessment in CARICOM Member States and Associate Member States.
instruments.summary: Regional policy framework of the Caribbean Examinations Council, a CARICOM institution, on responsible use of generative AI in secondary education and CXC assessment. It sets principles on academic integrity, ethical and inclusive AI education, curriculum integration (labelling and citing AI-generated material), teacher training, bias mitigation, data privacy with parental consent, infrastructure, human oversight of AI used in assessment decisions, psychosocial impact and assessment access for learners with special needs, and assigns responsibilities to regional bodies (COHSOD, CXC, CAPSS, CUT, UWI) and national Ministries of Education and CXC committees.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Regional framework for responsible generative AI use in secondary education and examinations.

leads.title: CTU Caribbean AI Task Force (CAITF) Final Report: Toward Harmonized AI Policies and Recommendations for the Caribbean (July 2026)
leads.note: Seven-pillar advisory framework (data and compute; governance, ethics and standards anchored in the UNESCO Recommendation; economy; talent; public-sector AI; disaster resilience; regional leadership). The task force was created under a mandate of the CTU 31st General Conference of Ministers (Oct 2025); the report states no endorsement by CTU ministers or CARICOM organs and calls itself an advisory framework. An interim draft for consultation was released on 13 Dec 2025 (https://ctu.int/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/CCAITF-Draft-Interim-Report-MASTER.pdf). To be recorded if the CTU General Conference or CARICOM COTED or Heads of Government endorse it. An April 2026 copy also exists at /2026/04/CAITF-Final-Report.pdf (not compared).

leads.note: The Secretariat's AI category pages (19 posts, Dec 2024-Oct 2026) carry speeches, workshops, CARICOM-UNDP AI capacity-building (Nov 2025) and a democracy-and-AI statement (3 Jul 2026), but no AI declaration, framework or policy text. The Heads of Government key-outcomes page of Feb 2026 has no AI item. The Strategic Framework for Regional Digital Resilience 2025-2030 (approved by Heads in July 2024) and the Regional Digital Development Strategy were not located; check them for an AI pillar.

leads.title: Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court AI policy or practice direction (announced January 2026)
leads.note: The Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court is the court of the Organisation of Eastern Caribbean States (OECS), not a CARICOM institution; listed here because the site has no OECS page. Known from news only (opening of the 2026 law year, 13 Jan 2026): the Court plans an AI policy for courtrooms. No AI practice direction found on eccourts.org, and the Civil Procedure Rules 2023 copies on gov.ai contain no AI provisions in the parts read. To be recorded once an official dated text appears.
